See Setup Assistant listing when first-run OOBE wizard UI is your lead — not .mobileconfig profile editors. What Apple Configuration Profiles actually do — listing honesty

Apple supports Configuration Profiles as signed .mobileconfig payload files that deliver settings to iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV — Wi-Fi credentials, VPN configurations, certificates, restrictions, email accounts, web clips, and other MDM-managed settings. IT admins distribute profiles through MDM servers, Apple Configurator during device prep, or manual installation when users consent in Settings. Third-party MDM and device-management apps may complement this by authoring profiles, signing payloads, or educating fleet admins about classic profile distribution. Configuration Profile–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

Classic MDM profile marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Configuration Profiles — not a literal paste of US marketing:

配置描述文件 (Configuration Profile)

Apple's Chinese MDM and enterprise support materials use 配置描述文件 for signed .mobileconfig payload files that deliver settings to managed devices. Technical marketing may also use 描述文件 as shorthand on dashboard frames. AppLocale picks the term IT admins recognize on each screenshot — a profile editor frame needs 配置描述文件-friendly phrasing; a technical badge may keep .mobileconfig when accurate to your English source.

mobileconfig / .mobileconfig

The .mobileconfig file extension is widely recognized by MDM buyers globally. zh-Hans marketing often keeps mobileconfig or .mobileconfig on technical frames that show file export, signing, or payload schema editors — alongside 配置描述文件 for buyer-facing benefit copy.

Wi-Fi 描述文件 (Wi-Fi profile)

Configuration Profiles commonly deliver corporate Wi-Fi credentials and network settings. zh-Hans copy uses Wi-Fi 描述文件 or 无线局域网描述文件 on frames that explain fleet Wi-Fi deployment — distinct from Personal Hotspot 个人热点 consumer tethering marketing.

VPN 描述文件 (VPN profile)

MDM platforms push VPN settings through Configuration Profile payloads. zh-Hans marketing uses VPN 描述文件 when your English source genuinely markets VPN profile authoring or distribution — not generic "secure every connection" overclaims your screenshots do not support.

证书描述文件 (certificate profile)

Identity and S/MIME certificates often ship inside Configuration Profiles. zh-Hans copy uses 证书描述文件 on frames that show certificate payload editors or PKI deployment workflows — separate from Passkeys or Security Keys consumer authentication marketing.

限制描述文件 (restrictions payload)

Supervised and managed devices receive app, content, and feature restrictions through profile payloads. zh-Hans marketing uses 限制描述文件 or 访问限制 when your English source markets restrictions payloads — not Screen Time usage caps unless that is what the screenshot shows.

AppLocale FAQ

What are Apple Configuration Profiles and why does listing copy matter?

Configuration Profiles are installable .mobileconfig payload files that deliver Wi-Fi, VPN, certificates, restrictions, and other settings to managed devices through MDM, Apple Configurator, or Settings. Marketing those payloads on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does profile authoring or .mobileconfig support auto-translate my China listing?

No. Configuration Profiles are classic MDM payload files — they do not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

What listing fields does AppLocale rewrite for Configuration Profile apps?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines that mention Configuration Profiles, .mobileconfig files, or profile payloads — rewritten from your English originals with terms like 配置描述文件, 描述文件, and Wi-Fi 描述文件 where accurate.

How is this different from DDM, Configurator, enrollment flows, or Guided Access?

Configuration Profile listing copy markets installable .mobileconfig payload files and classic profile distribution. DDM listing copy markets the modern MDM configuration protocol. Configurator listing copy markets Mac desktop device preparation. ADUE and Setup Assistant listing copy market enrollment workflows. Guided Access listing copy markets single-app kiosk lock. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature.

How is this different from Return to Service, Activation Lock, Find My, or Lockdown Mode?

Configuration Profiles push settings payloads to managed devices. Return to Service erases supervised devices for fleet redeployment. Activation Lock prevents consumer reactivation without the owner's Apple ID after erase. Find My and Lost Mode help locate missing devices. Lockdown Mode is extreme cyberattack hardening. Each is a separate Apple feature — do not reuse boilerplate across them.

Does AppLocale author .mobileconfig files or configure MDM servers?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. Profile authoring, MDM engineering, and Activation Lock bypass are outside AppLocale scope. We rewrite how you describe existing Configuration Profile workflows on the store page — we do not sign profiles at runtime.

What character limits apply to zh-Hans Configuration Profile fields?

App name and subtitle are each up to 30 characters. Keywords allow up to 100 characters. Description and screenshot caption lines have longer limits but should stay concise — especially overlays that must fit on-device mockups.
